speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history. To better understand your condition, could you please describe the nature of your chest pain and tell me if you've noticed any blood in your vomit? Also, have you experienced any recent travel or changes in your diet?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to check if you have a foreign body lodged in your airway or esophagus; have you been able to swallow saliva since the choking episode, and do you feel like something is stuck in your throat? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Neck_X-Ray. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture) secondary to forceful vomiting.
